claims.claim_text: The indexed Leslie H. Atlass Jr. is strongly matched to H. Leslie Atlass Jr., promoted to major while serving overseas with the Army in 1944.
claims.evidence_excerpt: promotion of his son H. Leslie Atlass, Jr., to the rank of Major ... overseas with the Army
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary radio-industry notice reports H. Leslie Atlass Jr.'s promotion to major during overseas Army service; an FCC report independently confirms his wartime Army service and Chicago background.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the unusual surname, suffix, inverted first and middle names, exact major rank, wartime Army service, and Chicago family context align across the index, contemporary notice, and official FCC biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: The evidence confirms a wartime Army identity but identifies no pre-service employer. The FCC employment chronology begins after his 1945 discharge and is not repurposed as pre-OSS evidence.
claims.match_notes: The FCC page's OCR renders Atlass once as Attlass; the contemporary 1944 notice and index preserve Atlass. No employer is inferred from his father's CBS position.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Aldon N. Attayer is strongly matched to Aldon N. D. Attayer, a Pennsylvania resident whose 1944 Allied Control Commission survey is cited in scholarship.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Aldon N. Attayer, Survey of Jewish internment camp at Campagna, 17 marzo 1944
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A 1942 federal patent gives the rare name Aldon N. D. Attayer and a Pennsylvania residence; a scholarly footnote cites a 1944 Allied Control Commission survey by Aldon N. Attayer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: a highly distinctive name, matching N. initial, 1942 federal record, and exact-name authorship of a March 1944 Allied Control Commission report align with the indexed Army major. The extra D. initial is retained as a documented variant.
claims.temporal_assessment: The records establish dated prewar and wartime activities but do not name an employer immediately before OSS or establish that patent authorship was employment.
claims.match_notes: The cited RG 331 item should be reviewed directly. The patent is not treated as self-employment, and the survey is not yet modeled as a formal military or government assignment because its authorship context remains indirect.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Paul R. Attix is probably the private listed in the Ninth Army's contemporary unit history.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1947 Ninth Army unit history includes Paul R. Attix in its private roster, matching the rare exact name and enlisted grade printed in the OSS index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable: the uncommon exact name and closely matching enlisted grade support the match, but the unit-history roster does not reproduce the indexed private identifier or directly state an OSS connection.
claims.temporal_assessment: The roster establishes wartime Army service but does not show whether Ninth Army service preceded, followed, or overlapped the OSS record and supplies no civilian employment evidence.
claims.match_notes: Published only as a qualified identity lead. Box 25 and official Army records are needed before modeling Ninth Army as a pre-OSS assignment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Roy B. Attride Sr. is confirmed as Pfc Roy R. B. Attride Sr., an OSS X-2 Insurance Unit leader in the European Theater.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Pfc Roy R. B. Attride, Sr. ... Succeeded Major Rushin as head of Insurance Unit
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An official OSS commendation record names Pfc Roy R. B. Attride Sr., describes his X-2 Insurance Unit leadership, and says he represented OSS on a British joint-intelligence subcommittee.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed: the official NARA document supplies the rare full surname, Roy and B. names, senior suffix, Private First Class rank, and direct OSS service; Grenfell's 1945 alumni notice independently places Roy Attride in Army and OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The claim establishes wartime OSS service and identity. It does not by itself identify the affiliation immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: The index prints one B. while the OSS document gives R. B.; both original forms remain visible. The extra initial is treated as a documented variant, not a silent correction.

claims.claim_text: Roy R. B. Attride was selected as the St. Anthony District office bookkeeper on the Grenfell Association's permanent staff for winter 1936-37.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: The association's July 1936 staff report names Roy R. B. Attride as bookkeeper in its St. Anthony office; its 1943 alumni news calls Roy Attride a former staff member.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The rare full R. B. name, senior-suffix wartime evidence, institutional former-staff notice, 1945 Army/OSS notice, and official OSS X-2 record establish that the staff member is the indexed person.
claims.temporal_assessment: The staff report explicitly dates the appointment to winter 1936-37, well before wartime OSS service. No accessible source shows that it was the immediate predecessor or last civilian employment.
claims.match_notes: This is published only as earlier documented pre-OSS employment. It is excluded from immediate-affiliation and last-civilian-employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Commander Amariah G. Atwater is strongly matched to Amariah George Cox Atwater Sr., documented in an OSS naval-officer personnel-card series.

claims.evidence_paraphrase: A NARA finding aid begins its naval officer personnel-card range with Amariah G. C. Atwater; a separate local-history biography expands the name and assigns him an OSS Middle Eastern Theater leadership role.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: the exceptionally rare first name and surname, matching G. initial, added C. initial, Lieutenant Commander classification, direct OSS naval-officer card context, and secondary wartime role align.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish identity and wartime OSS context but do not date the listed Wrigley role relative to OSS. No pre-OSS employer claim is published.
